# Draft:Christopher N. Warren

----
Christopher N. Warren is Head of English and Professor of English and History (by courtesy) at Carnegie Mellon University. A leader in computational humanities, he has held faculty and visiting scholar positions at Oxford University, the University of Chicago, University College London, and the National University of Ireland-Galway.
Warren co-leads Carnegie Mellon's computational humanities initiative and is the author of Literature and the Law of Nations, 1580-1680 (Oxford University Press), which was awarded the Roland H. Bainton Prize for Literature. His peer-reviewed journal publications have appeared in Shakespeare Quarterly, Milton Studies, Digital Humanities Quarterly, The European Journal of International Law, English Literary Renaissance, and conference proceedings in computer science, including the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI), the International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR), and the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL). With Daniel Shore, Warren co-founded the NEH-funded [http://www.sixdegreesoffrancisbacon.com/ Six Degrees of Francis Bacon] project and with Max G'Sell and Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick created [https://github.com/chrisvvarren/Print-Probability Print & Probability], funded by the NSF and NEH, which uses machine learning and artificial intelligence to discover and center the anonymous craftsmen and -women responsible for printing controversial clandestine materials in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Warren recently delivered the Sol. M. and Mary Ann O'Brian Malkin Lecture at the University of Virginia Rare Book School on the topic, [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ElvNacFyoWQ "What is Computational Bibliography?"]
Warren's Print & Probability project was selected as a 2025 [https://www.schmidtsciences.org/havi-2025-announcement/ Humanities and AI Virtual Institute (HAVI) awardee] by Schmidt Sciences. Recognized projects are those working to develop AI tools that deepen our understanding of human history and culture. Print & Probability is a project that uses artificial intelligence to uncover the secret printers who produced controversial books in early modern Europe.
Warren lives in Pittsburgh, PA and is married to landscape architect Julie Kachniasz. The couple has three children.
